findings.description: The README reports 1,158,924 submitted bytes for the linked 1,000-entry fixture, but sync-before.json and an independent rerun both report 1,158,807. The former number belongs to the initial audit fixture, whose empty case also differs from the reusable verifier.
findings.smallestFix: Change README.md:43 to 1,158,807, or explicitly attribute 1,158,924 to the distinct initial audit fixture. No source change needed.

objections.topic: Serialized recovery snapshot and comparison work
objections.evidence: The source-local probe observes four complete recovery JSON.stringify calls in an unchanged 1,000-entry cycle, each returning 422,107 UTF-16 code units, 1,688,428 code units in total for this fixture. persistedLocal retains one snapshot across awaits and each capture creates a candidate string. These counts do not measure physical allocations, GC, CPU or peak memory.
objections.assessment: String snapshots avoid the mutable shallow-alias bug that an object reference or shallow copy would introduce. persistedLocal changes only after a successful awaited storage write. The cycle-local value is not an instance/global cache. Removing snapshots, adding hashes or restructuring validated-model contracts would add risk or move costs without measurement. Keep the guard provisionally; measure before calling it an overall efficiency win.

objections.status: Inherited boundary assumption, not a regression from this diff
objections.evidence: Synthetic rejection-before-write, recovery-only partial write, store-only partial write and both-written-then-rejected produce identical baseline/candidate outcomes. All preserve Remote edit after retry except recovery-only: if the final recovery baseline commits but STORE_KEY does not, the next cycle interprets the old store as a new local edit and publishes Personal. This behavior also exists in isolated git HEAD.
objections.assessment: The submitted failed-apply test models rejection before either key writes and passes. It does not prove crash atomicity across storage keys. Do not describe that test as proof of arbitrary partial-write recovery. If actual Chrome storage semantics permit recovery-only commit, a separate journal/commit protocol or explicit storage transaction guarantee is required. This review did not establish that the artificial failure is reachable in Chrome.

objections.status: No introduced defect found under awaited completion semantics
objections.assessment: A post-cycle check prevents creation after disposal; the post-create check clears late creation. Serial drain prevents overlapping cycle alarm changes. The tests cover three cycle completion phases and pending creation. A Promise that resolves before its underlying alarm operation takes effect would violate the assumed API completion contract; the fixture and source review cannot establish native IPC ordering. Cross-install ownership of a shared alarm name and ignored alarm rejections predate these edits.

objections.topic: Folder-state semantics and transient index cost
objections.assessment: 400 seeded differential cases match baseline, including duplicate folder IDs across and within spaces and unusual expansion values. remaining.delete preserves first match within each space, and later spaces overwrite earlier matches. The zero-folder branch skips scanning; scanning stops when every relevant folder is found. folderIds, per-space Set and localExpansion add temporary JS objects; fewer pin reads are established, lower native RAM/CPU is not.
